To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the satisfiability problem for the following logics is PSPACE-complete: ALC with conjunction, negation of concepts, and general TBox axioms; and ALC with conjunction and negation of roles, and general Tbox axioms.
the satisfiability problem in ALC with Boolean restrictions is PTIME-complete in the presence of general axioms and PSPACE-complete in the presence in general axioms.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the concept satisfiability is tractable if the use of Boolean connectives is restricted to the conjunction and the disjunction of concepts, and intractable otherwise, even when axioms are not present.
satisfiability is PSPACE-complete for ALC with unrestricted axioms and EXPTIME-complete for ALC without axioms.
satisfiability for ALC with restricted use of Boolean operators is intractable if the use of negation is restricted, and it is tractable if negation is not restricted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the presence of Boolean operators, the satisfiability problem becomes hard in the presence of nominals, role inclusion axioms or axioms that contain a Boolean operator, and that it is tractable if the Boolean operators can only occur in the scope of a quantifier.
the presence of axiomatic knowledge in the sub-Boolean fragments of ALC leads to intractability, and this intractability cannot be avoided by restricting the form of the axioms.
, for the restricted Boolean fragments of ALC with or without axioms, the satisfiability problem is PSPACE-complete if the fragment is not too restricted and NP-complete otherwise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fragment of ALC with a tractable concept satisfiability problem is not necessarily a fragment of any of the aforementioned tractable logics.
the presence of axiomatic knowledge is crucial to obtain intractable cases of satisfiability in the presence of restrictions to the use of Boolean connectives.
the presence of Boolean operators in ALC is not necessarily problematic, as long as they are not used to encode a Boolean function.
